tagline.text: Regent of the solar system, owner of the broadcast, and the company that chose a dungeon as the way Earth gets its matter back.
Runs the show on the cheap, holds the foreclosure on Earth, and gets one veto a season.

beats.headline: The foreclosure
beats.text: It claims Earth under Syndicate law and turns the planet into a mining claim. The dungeon is the legal cover and the revenue at once.

beats.headline: It burns a veto rather than pay
beats.text: Eighty-three Celestial boxes are owed. Borant appeals, a Syndicate court overrules it, and it burns its one seasonal veto to void the prizes anyway, which has never been done this early. It is still liable for the one box that was opened before the appeal. A production company that cheap has seams worth looking for.

entities.name: The Syndicate
entities.tagline: Three billion star systems, the rules Earth was seized under, and the audience for all of this.

beats.headline: Three billion star systems
beats.text: Over three billion independent star systems. Its rules are the ones Earth was seized under, and every season a new Dungeon Crawler World debuts across its net for quintillions of citizens to become obsessed with. It is the law and the audience at once.

beats.headline: Seven factions lose in court
beats.text: Seven factions sue to take the Gate of the Feral Gods from Carl, naming him and the AI as co-defendants, and the Syndicate Court finds for the defence. He collects seven Fight the Power achievements, stock certificates, and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers.

beats.headline: A headquarters in Florida
beats.text: The Syndicate's presence in the system now runs out of a temporary headquarters on the Eastern Seaboard of North America, with Prime Minister Victory and her staff. They chose an area they believed had minimal surviving native life, somewhere in the state of Florida, and the moment they set down the natives were all over them. Orbit belongs to the Open Intellect Action Network, and Borant has nobody spare to watch the feeds. For now, it is busy.

beats.headline: A suicide mission, from security
beats.text: Captain Fresh of Syndicate security says it plainly to the soldier going in under a dead fan's name: it is a suicide mission. The Syndicate is trying to nuke the whole system off the map before it spreads further, and losing; the AI stops everything and answers in kind. A surgical crawler kill, they believe, will destabilise the group, start the Ascendency game early and let their other assets move. It is us or them, he says. The viewers who will not stop watching are to blame too.

entities.name: The Royal Court of Princess Donut
entities.tagline: Named by a cat on the first floor, on the grounds that she had the highest stat total and nobody could stop her.

beats.headline: Formally inaugurated
beats.text: Party leadership goes to the highest stat total. Her first act with it is to rename the party after herself. On a show, a name the audience will repeat is not a joke — it is an asset.

beats.headline: Seventh in the first heat
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut crosses the finish line of heat one in seventh place, with Team Free Love's wrecked minivan chained behind the food truck on a flatbed Carl built at the side of the road. The bleachers are empty. The results: One Fine Pig, the Jugglers, the Lady Dominators and the Gimp, the Wild Hunt, Girth the Trouble, Team Sparkles, the Court, and Free Love eighth. The Trauco Triplets are eliminated. One team down, and only one.

beats.headline: Last in heat two
beats.text: Seventh of seven finishers in Heat Two, behind everyone still racing, with Girth the Trouble the only team eliminated. The court did most of the work on Prison Pocket, spent a small crowd of summoned gremlins doing it, and watched the Pontiac and the armoured truck drive past its leader while he lay in the road. Princess Donut calls it an apt metaphor for what always happens when they do all the heavy lifting. Carl says it could be worse. The costume disagrees.

beats.headline: First place, in pieces
beats.text: Heat Three: first place, the Royal Court of Princess Donut, which crossed the line upside down in a food truck that is now spread across the road along with its tater tots. Both hired ghouls are dead. The Wild Hunt and the Jugglers are eliminated, two teams gone in the one heat, and a replacement is coming for the empty sixth garage. Gremlins with carts and wheelbarrows come out of garages one and three to collect what is left of the truck.

beats.headline: First in heat four
beats.text: Heat Four. First place, the Royal Court of Princess Donut, driven for the last stretch by a dead camel, after a run of clockwork toads. Second, the Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Third, Team Flamengo. Fourth, Team Free Love. Fifth, team Sparkles. One Fine Pig is eliminated. The next track is a screw factory, steel mill and doll workshop, and containment theft is now on.

beats.headline: Second place in heat six
beats.text: Heat six results: first, Team Sparkles, driving itself while its unicorn sleeps it off. Second, the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Third, Team Flamengo, which is Crawler Osvaldo, who told the chat he was about to cross the line when he was not, and so is alive, over the line with a minute to spare. Eliminated: Team Free Love, whose van lies wrecked in the hallway short of the finish. The Court drives past it. The princess climbs into Carl's lap and stays there.

entities.name: Meadow Lark
entities.tagline: An elder care facility whose residents came down the stairs together and kept going.

beats.headline: Imani, Yolanda, the Andrews brothers, and Agatha
beats.text: Carl and Donut find them on the first floor. Tales are exchanged, plans are formed, and the Royal Court agrees to keep helping them.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and Donut take it down out of the redoubt. Agatha is in the room for it, bleeding from the head and doing nothing, which still counts for experience.

tagline.text: Hekla's group: Icelandic, crossbows and breastplates, and growing.
Hekla's group, and the one Katia came in with.

beats.headline: They carry her as far as they can
beats.text: A neighbourhood boss and a borough boss with Katia in tow, until the third floor scatters everyone on arrival and she is too far from the rest of them to share in the experience.

entities.name: The Blood Sultanate
entities.tagline: A royal house on the ninth floor whose succession a cat joined by accident on the first.

beats.headline: Named in the crown's warning
beats.text: Every royal in the line must kill the Sultan and every other member of the family before descending to the tenth floor.

tagline.text: A hundred and fifty men with rifles, down to eighty and counting their bullets.
Arrived as a recap segment and left as a wipe.

beats.headline: Named on the recap
beats.text: The armed men from Africa get a name on the broadcast, and a graphic counting what is left of their ammunition.

beats.headline: Wiped
beats.text: Another recap carries the news: a city boss kills every one of them except a single man locked outside the boss room, and the remaining-crawler count drops below a million in the same broadcast.

entities.name: The Princess Posse
entities.tagline: Fifty thousand retired crawlers who came back in, under the banner of a cat.

beats.headline: They are already there when he walks in
beats.text: Rosetta, Tipid, Justice Light and fifty thousand others have signed on. Carl gets emotional.

beats.headline: Digging in
beats.text: NPCs and former crawlers build the defences together: the changelings and the flesh golems started the stronghold, and a few thousand of the newcomers chose the Fortification Engineer race so they could build fast and level while they do it.

tagline.text: Bald, pale elves with a territory of their own marked on the hunters' map of the grounds.
Half the food in the universe belongs to them, along with the entertainment channels, and they have a contract they intend to see honoured.
Their warlord is dead and their army is off the board.

beats.headline: A hunter of theirs, and the map on his body
beats.text: The group takes one of their hunters down and Carl loots him: an Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea, and a crude map of the hunting grounds with a territory marked for every outfit working them. That is the first honest look anyone gets at how the hunt is organised. The Hive and the Skull Empire have both put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Dream have their own reasons for being here.

beats.headline: Elves at the door
beats.text: Two or three of the elves get a catapult set up and walk gas-rock artillery across the town. Carl uses Samantha to deliver missiles, delivers a villain's soliloquy while he is at it, and puts down another of their hunters.

beats.headline: They buy a storyline instead of fighting for one
beats.text: Quasar has the warning ready before the sixty-hour ceasefire is out. The Dream have bought out the Vengeance of the Daughter and are pressing for fulfilment of the guaranteed third season written into it. An entertainment company, bought and aimed at a crawler.

beats.headline: They walk out of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan goes with them. What is left of the alliance is the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers, which is a smaller thing than it was that morning.

beats.headline: Epitome Tagg is dead, the Dream is finished
beats.text: Emberus wants Samantha interrogated and intends to break the floor in sixty-six minutes whatever the answer. In the middle of that, the Dream is beaten. Epitome Tagg is dead. Two teams remain standing on this floor, the Princess Posse and Team Retribution, and neither of them is the one that owned half the food in the universe.

tagline.text: Caprids. They own the tunnelling system, which is why anything that happens down here can be watched anywhere at all.
Carl's sponsor now. A full-grown goat stood in front of the cameras for fifteen seconds, bleated, and was gone.
Not a collective mind. A herd, and a herd bolts, which is why their matriarch treats a piece of news the way anyone else treats a loaded weapon.

beats.headline: The tunnelling system
beats.text: Mordecai catches the team up on the shape of the wider universe, and two powers come out of it: the Apothecary, and the Plenty. The Plenty built the tunnelling system a few hundred seasons ago and kept it proprietary. Before it, most of the universe got the crawl on a delay of anything from an hour to a year. Prosperity, in other words, is a thing they sell.

beats.headline: The vacated sponsorship goes to them
beats.text: Carl signs autographs with the Popov brothers, poses for photographs with a fan who has a head tentacle named Maggie and strong views on the eradication of cocker spaniels, and finds out on the same afternoon who has bought him. The Plenty.

beats.headline: Two sponsors, one gift
beats.text: The Plenty and the Apothecary each send Carl and Donut something that protects them against vampirism, and they arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to compare notes. These two plainly do.

beats.headline: Carl works out who arranged it
beats.text: Kiwi and her dinosaurs arrive, Donut charms her with a potion, and somewhere in the middle of it Carl sees the shape of the thing: his own sponsor set the chain of events up, and wanted Miriam Dom to die at the end of it. A benefactor box is not a gift. It is a production note with a bow on it.

beats.headline: The herd finds out
beats.text: The goats start to panic and faint, certain the end times have come. Gamori, the matriarch, had known all of it and told none of them, because she knew precisely this would happen. Harbinger arrives to point out that he warned her, that he has been protecting the herd the whole time, and that they expelled him for it anyway.

beats.headline: The tunnels are not theirs
beats.text: The Plenty announce that they have lost control of the tunnel network outside the center system. Sydnee Iglacia, on air, calls it the first of the nine attacks: control. Gods from the dungeon keep appearing near the nodes, the checkpoints into the center system are overwhelmed, and the one place in the galaxy that still looks safe is the center. Prime Minister Victory is not so sure.

tagline.text: One of the oldest and largest of the system governments, orcish, rich on weapons, and famously bad at letting an insult go.
Its army is at the wall on the ninth floor and its king has come with it.
The books are not its own. A financial criminal lives inside the empire and pays handsomely for the address.

beats.headline: Carl plants a seed on Danger Zone
beats.text: A few minutes of provocation on a chat show, and the Skull Empire answers them with a pulse from Prince Stalwart's yacht. It hits Manasa's trailer instead of Carl's, which was a mistake, and the Valtay answer that in turn by destroying the yacht, with his mother and the Maestro rumoured to be aboard. Three funerals come of it.

beats.headline: A claim staked on the hunters' map
beats.text: The map off the dead hunter divides the hunting grounds between the outfits working them, and two of those outfits have put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Hive is one. The Skull Empire is the other.

beats.headline: King Rust at the wall
beats.text: The enemy's northern army masses at the edge of camp, and riding in at the head of the orcs, in full battle parade regalia, is the king himself. The Posse closes off the saferoom before anybody can drop a bomb through its door. Rust asks for an official parlay.

beats.headline: The parlay, and what his daughter told the Syndicate
beats.text: Rust explains it himself. Princess Formidable has commandeered one of his own warships and announced that she means to trip the Failsafe by hand. She has also told the Syndicate that the empire builds secret back doors into the security systems it sells. He asks Carl to send her a message on behalf of the people of Earth and trades a retreat for it. Rosetta takes his head off with a whip as he rides away, and the army charges.

beats.headline: Zev's aside, and Rosetta on Harry Tisch
beats.text: While the teams build their floats, Zev mentions in passing that Odette's husband has bought the rights to every show Donut has ever mentioned, and that it is probably all that is keeping the orcs solvent. Rosetta supplies the rest: his name is Harry Tisch, King Rust vetoed his extradition for tax fraud, and he has been working himself deeper into the empire ever since. Empires that sell weapons still have to bank somewhere.

beats.headline: Rent, tripled
beats.text: With D'Nadia dead, whoever is running the Skull Empire in the royal family's absence has swallowed every real estate holding of a group the Prism controlled. In the Makoka Cloud, Sydnee Iglacia's rent triples starting the next crutch, and oxygen is no longer included. She curses the Skull Empire, the Valtay and D'Nadia in the same breath.

tagline.text: A tax-exempt outfit nobody has heard of, which just won a sponsorship slot in a bidding war that ran to the final microsecond.
Crawlers who got out, and who want the whole thing stopped. Fifty thousand of them have come back in.
Every ship in orbit is theirs.

beats.headline: Carl's second sponsor
beats.text: Donut is taken by Veriluxx RealPet Companions and Katia by the Squim Conglomerate, and neither of those needs explaining: a pet brand wants the cat, a conglomerate wants the coverage. Carl is taken by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, which is registered as a not-for-conquest, answers to no system government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.

beats.headline: One root vegetable
beats.text: The Valtay Corporation sends a neural enhancer, which is exactly the sort of thing a corporation sends. The Network sends a single Toraline root vegetable. Mordecai has never seen the plant, and can only guess at what it is for: a potion, an explosive, an inside joke. It is listed as very rare and worth about as much as an old shirt.

beats.headline: A potion and a note in code
beats.text: Signet warns that the dryads may call Diwata against the spreading brambles. Then a potion turns up in the benefactor box with a note that says only 'Save the toraline', until Carl's Escape Plan shows him the rest: Circe has sponsored Diwata, the potion is for Donut, and it is signed P. Hu. Whoever writes these has a view of the board that nobody standing on it has.

beats.headline: The first time a sponsor asks for something
beats.text: The request arrives through Zev, and it is a request rather than a present: go on Shadow Boxer. Carl agrees to it, reluctantly. Sponsors are supposed to send prizes and buy airtime. They are not supposed to want a favour.

beats.headline: They take the orbit
beats.text: Lexis has the news and cannot get to the end of it. The Open Intellect Action Network has taken over every ship in orbit, and a third party she will not name has appeared at the kinder facility and is protecting it, confused. Then a message reaches her, and she stops talking, and she is afraid.

relations.note: Doctor Hu built the Crawler Project first; the Network is the half that wants the crawl stopped.

tagline.text: A democratic government of many races, whose army had a castle dropped on it before the season had properly started.
Caught cheating on the ninth floor, punished for it, and short one commander who took his own way out.

beats.headline: A castle lands on their army
beats.text: Quasar brings Carl the state of his ninth-floor team, and the state of it is that the castle came down in the middle of the Lemig Sortion's army. His people got clear and are building their own stronghold instead. The Lemig Sortion are the ones with a building in their camp.

beats.headline: Carl wakes up in their base
beats.text: Eleven hours gone, blood all over him, and most of the room around him killed by the thing riding inside him. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness had been arranging something together. It has come apart on top of them.

beats.headline: The field ruling
beats.text: Carl, Commander Stockade, Architect Houston and their adjutants convene for an official adjudication, and it goes on the record. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness used outside information to time a Summon Ally, meaning to pull Carl bodily to their base so that what was in him could be let loose on the rest of the Princess Posse. They got half of him, and the other half of the plan.

beats.headline: Punished, and the ceasefire ends early
beats.text: Panford, their adjutant, is left to explain the rampage through the base to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye, lost his mind, and finished it himself. Ferdinand gets an emergency action item passed for a live feed blackout so nobody can do this again. The Lemig Sortion is punished for cheating, the ceasefire ends early, and Carl goes home.

tagline.text: Their pets arrive before they do: a swarm of Dumplins, every one of them carrying the Gurgles.
Several races who traded away everything but the brain for machinery, and kept going.
Warlord Fang hid inside his own pet, and the castle came down on the pair of them.

beats.headline: Rot stickers with the Gurgles
beats.text: The southern defence is already holding against the Dream, the Prism and the Nagas when the Reavers make their contribution: a horde of their own pet rot stickers, raised by hand to trust their masters, then juiced, infected and turned loose. This is a power that fights by handing you something diseased and standing back.

beats.headline: Carl gets the background on them
beats.text: Tina rampages, the compromised mages are put down, and somewhere in the middle of that Carl finally hears what a Reaver actually is. The real ones are all machine, with a little biological brain hidden somewhere inside the shell, and they can reshape themselves out of nanobot-sized parts. Anyone not vat-born who wants the citizenship gives up their biological form to get in the door and works off every upgrade after that.

beats.headline: What is left of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan and the Dream leave the alliance. That leaves the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers holding it, and the Reavers are not the sort of partner anyone chose.

beats.headline: The castle, the dragon and Fang
beats.text: The Reavers' robot dogs come at the rescue team inside the castle. Juice Box finds Louis, possesses him, teleports him out and leaves a heap of No Disassembles where he had been. Carl sets them off. The castle goes, the dragon goes, and Fang goes with it, hiding inside his own pet. Then Juice Box says the rest of it: they had been operating on Louis, and the heart and lungs he has now hold pieces of Epitome Tagg.

tagline.text: A name used as an insult: nobody in the Skull Clan wants to be mistaken for one.
Showrunners once. They ran the first crawl ever to lose money, and have not run a season since.
Cobra-headed, ruled out of the Blood Sultanate, and part of the push on the southern line.
The poverty was a performance. There were plans for the shipbuilding yards underneath it.
A signed offer on the table: citizenship for every native of Earth, in exchange for room in Earth's system.

beats.headline: In the southern push
beats.text: Carl and Donut join the defence in the south, and across the no-man's-land the Nagas hold the line beside the Dream and the Prism. Cobra-headed, and playing under the name of the Blood Sultanate, taken from a bloodier time in their own history.

beats.headline: Prepotente takes their army apart
beats.text: Elle brings the count back. Most of the Naga army is already dead, and one goat did it, as payment for what the Blood Hunter show did to Miriam Dom. Baroness Victory tells Carl he cannot work with him directly unless he signs on properly.

beats.headline: The airship at their castle
beats.text: Louis and Donut come at the Naga castle from the air. Elle and Imani go in on foot. Katia tells Carl that if this goes badly she wants him to have the flower, so that Donut at least reaches the next floor. Prepotente arrives to meet them.

beats.headline: Never broke at all
beats.text: Time freezes for the AI to announce the fight, and it uses the moment to tell everyone watching that outside the dungeon the Nagas had only been pretending to be poor. There were secret plans to seize the shipbuilding facilities. Then time restarts and the fight happens anyway.

beats.headline: Rishi's offer
beats.text: Their prisoner explains the Great Consensus, and that Vinata held to it, and that Vinata's group meant to steal the Naga fleet and leave the central system for good. Then he offers a signed document: citizenship in Naga lands for every native of Earth, if the Nagas may settle the other planets in Earth's system. Carl marks him with the ring and kills him.

beats.headline: Widow's Rights
beats.text: Outside the crawl, a bloody coup has put a new Sultan on the Naga throne, and his niece Chandra, one of Rishi's widows, has found a use for an old law: a royal widow may claim her husband's killer as her new husband. A public jury in Naga court found the idea of punishing Carl this way amusing and voted it through, adding the holdings of the defeated as his wedding gift in a fan box. As his wife she signs for him, she has filed to put Princess Donut's earnings under his conservatorship, and two Taurin associates have been paid to call on Quasar.

tagline.text: The ninth floor's own people, fielded as the defending team, and allied with the crawlers from the first hour of it.
Their warlord turned into an Unwashed on camera and told the audience that it is coming for them all.
One of two teams still standing at the end of the war.

beats.headline: The defending team names itself
beats.text: Carl and Donut come onto the ninth floor at Larracos, at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire, and the defending side already has a name it chose for itself. Cascadia runs through the rules. The crawlers ally with it against the Bloc, which is every other faction on the board.

beats.headline: Ferdinand holds the interface
beats.text: Juice Box and Louis are reunited, and he is visibly uneasy about the marriage. Then she lays out the practical problem: Ferdinand is mayor of Shanty Town, just outside Larracos, and he holds the warlord interface for the team, because he is technically from outside. Nothing this side of the wall moves without a cat's cooperation. Drick is the adjutant.

beats.headline: It is coming for you all
beats.text: Odette arrives to replace Chaco, Cascadia comes apart on air, and Carl spends an emergency action item to shut the communication loophole the other teams have been using. Then Juice Box turns into an Unwashed in front of the cameras and tells everyone watching that it is coming for them all.

beats.headline: Two teams left
beats.text: Epitome Tagg is dead and the Dream is beaten, which leaves the Princess Posse and Team Retribution on the board. A team of NPCs was put on this floor to be fodder. It has outlasted eight galactic powers.

tagline.text: A collective mind spreading through the universe, and the thing the dungeon keeps drawing as the Krakaren.
Carl and Donut's third and final sponsor. Nobody on their side of it knows what she looks like.
One Primal who refused the collective, took the nine-tier attack, and is the reason anything biological is still here to watch this.

beats.headline: The truer translation
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the thing the Iron Tangle keeps caricaturing. Apothecary is the closer translation, taken from her ability to synthesise elements, and the dungeon's version bends the joke into an insult. She is a collective mind and she is spreading, which is a sentence that makes a great many people elsewhere nervous.

beats.headline: The third and final sponsor
beats.text: Clint has the account of Scolopendra's attack, and says the high elves were protected by something they had stolen. On the way back to Point Mongo the last sponsorship slot fills. The Apothecary takes it.

beats.headline: The same gift, the same day
beats.text: She and the Plenty each send protection against vampirism, and the two parcels arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to coordinate. Carl now has two who do.

beats.headline: The AI asks which side to take
beats.text: It wants advice from Orren and from Carl, and teleports Donut in as well, and it asks in a laboured metaphor about relationships: a girlfriend who looks like Agatha, and an older woman who has been giving it pointers on getting stronger, both of whom want the same man in prison dead. Donut tells it to find out whether he is really good or really bad before doing anything, and even then to stay out of it unless it has no choice.

beats.headline: The whole of it, on stage
beats.text: The AI gives the account itself. The Primals were individuals once, and their society spread until the warring and the waste made them decide to end it and keep their minds in one collective instead. Those who refused fled. The Apothecary was born near the end, engineered to meld into the whole, and joined the resistance instead. The collective became a weapon aimed at every remaining scrap of biological life, and when it let off the nine-tier attack she stood in front of it, and what grew back afterwards grew back behind her.

tagline.text: Dungeon-born magic elementals who stopped taking orders, and took the Gate with them on the way out.
Holding the castle at Larracos, six hours from taking the floor, and conscripting gods to keep it.
They leave with exactly what they came for, and a warning about Agatha on the way out.

beats.headline: Stalwart explodes and the Gate goes with them
beats.text: Carl and Samantha come out of the Party Planner into Reaver territory. Stalwart teleports in beside Elle and the waiting portal with a squad of war mages, Akuma among them. Then the mages around him chant, and Stalwart explodes, and Akuma teleports out holding the Gate of the Feral Gods. The war mages conscripted under Stalwart are nobody's soldiers now. They are a faction, which the rules do not have a slot for.

beats.headline: Two co-warlords, and a god on a leash
beats.text: They hold the Larracos castle, and six hours of holding it would take the floor. Baroness Victory reads out two co-warlords, Akuma and Agatha, and Akuma is not pleased about it. The Gate goes onto the Midnight Market and comes back as potions, and the potions conscript Yarilo. Fopsy, adjutant for the Dream, has a theory: that Agatha now thinks the AI is a danger to the Eulogist and wants the ascendency game over so it can be shut down.

beats.headline: Agatha walks off her post
beats.text: The system deems Warlord Agatha to have abandoned her post, and nobody, the adjutants included, can say why. She is removed, and Akuma is named sole warlord of the rebellion.

beats.headline: They quit the floor
beats.text: Akuma tells the Warlord Chat that the war mages are done here. They never wanted the castle; they came to test the potions and to find the Scavenger's Daughter, who was hidden inside it, and she is with them now. First, though, he wants Carl and Donut to kill Agatha, who was forced on the rebellion to get it system access: she is an enemy to them all. Then he leaves the realm, and under this season's rules the rebellion is recorded as defeated.

beats.headline: Five left, and a home overrun
beats.text: The war mages had lived in the Pineapple Cabaret. They left deliberately, back to cold storage, to be brought into Faction Wars and find the Scavenger's Daughter, and in the few days they were gone their protection spells failed and it was overrun: shadow mimics, the Ogre Imperium's leftovers, and older things Agatha could wake. There are five of them left. Plan one was more mages, plan two an old ally in the Nothing. Carl is plan three.

entities.name: The Dark Hive
entities.tagline: A mantis hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and Carl is on its list.

beats.headline: The Hive is hunting you
beats.text: A hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and the message it sends Carl is a note knifed to the saferoom door and signed by Vrah: the Hive is hunting him, there will be nowhere to hide, and his death will not be quick.

tagline.text: A power outside Borant that answers an insult by taking a prince’s yacht apart with his family aboard, and does not explain itself afterwards.
A business that is also a nation, run by a parasite that pilots other people’s bodies, and it holds the paper on Borant’s debt.

beats.headline: A creditor with a seat at the table
beats.text: A corporate system government inside the Syndicate, which is to say a company that is also a country and answers to neither description when it is inconvenient. Its people are parasites in the literal sense, riding the bodies of other races. It holds the Borant Corporation’s debt, and it sends a crawler a neural enhancer, which is the sort of gift that is also a note.

beats.headline: The Emperator's bomb
beats.text: The Emperator of the Valtay fleet comes through the tunnel gate carrying a system-busting bomb, apparently waiting for the AI to be distracted. It was not distracted. It says so in the middle of a floor announcement, read aloud by a mudskipper who had no idea the text was coming, and adds that it makes no apologies about where that giant suicide bomb just ended up. It does not say where. A creditor who arrives with a bomb has stopped negotiating.

beats.headline: A royalty clause, and a worm
beats.text: Sydnee Iglacia's publisher is a subsidiary of a Valtay company, and her contract lets them hold her royalties for the whole of her natural life, payable to heirs only on proof of her good moral character. The payments can be accelerated, if she signs a Valtay life contract and lets a worm take her over after death. It is not something she would ever dream of doing. Until her rent tripled, anyway.

entities.name: The Guild of Suffering
entities.tagline: A cult you join by accident, the moment you accept a gift from something that would prefer to be worshipped.

beats.headline: Membership arrives with the tattoo
beats.text: The guild worships a demigod, and access is granted by a tattoo that anyone who uses one of its artefacts receives whether or not they went looking for a guild. Mordecai notes, in the tone of a man reading a pamphlet he did not ask for, that it also runs outreach centres.

relations.note: Use the artefact, take the tattoo, and you are a member.
